note: Owner anchors 2026-11-11: a regular looking roughly the right way spots a man standing still in the open at 300 m in about 5-15 s (base rate 0.07 per s: median 10 s); a man lying still in crops at 100 m is very hard to spot until he moves or fires. Chance per scan = 1 - exp(-rate x scan time); rate = base x (reference range / range)^2 x exposed size by posture x movement or firing x visibility along the line of sight x where he is looking x optic x skill x stress x light. Moving through vegetation shows at least 15 % of a man (plants move); firing at least 50 % (flash, dust). A man already seen is kept with 20 times the rate and forgotten after 6 s unseen. All game values for review in the spotting lab. A man keeps track of at most 6 enemies at a time (the nearest); others he has seen pass into what his side knows (contacts, M3.3).
